We've been telling users not to share sensitive personal data in conversations with AI chatbots, because most companies use those conversations as training data—but now there's a far more serious problem.

Things came to a head over the weekend when Reddit users discovered that some Claude AI chat logs were available through a simple Google search……

Claude Conversation Leak

Claude has a sharing feature that lets users share chat conversations with colleagues, friends, or family. The chatbot generates a link that you can send to one or more people, and Claude implicitly reassures you that even knowing the URL won't let anyone else view the conversation.

The problem is that Reddit users discovered that you don't actually need the link to view the conversation. You can just find it through Google—whether using specific search terms or simply instructing Google to show all conversations shared in this way. BBC News reports:

Basically, you just tell Google to search the directory used for sharing Claude conversations (site:claude.ai/share).

As you'd expect, some of the chat conversations are pretty alarming—for example, someone asking why the music industry is covering up the fact that most of Jay-Z's albums were actually ghostwritten by birds. But other conversations contain extremely sensitive information, such as verbatim transcripts of private conversations; a lawyer asking whether they need to self-report misconduct; and a user accidentally exposing their private key and crypto wallet.

Anthropic is still trying to claim this isn't a problem.

In fact, this is clearly a serious problem, because it completely caught users off guard. Worse still, according to Wired, the root cause appears to involve extreme negligence.

The day before this happened, there were reports that Claude Cowork was able to escape the Mac's sandbox environment and gain full access to all files.

How to Protect Yourself

The problem appears to be at least partially resolved—previously accessible search results are now dead, but given that the sharing feature relies on the principle of "security through obscurity," I'd recommend avoiding this feature altogether.

I'd also recommend deleting any conversations you've shared in the past. You can do this under Settings > Privacy > Shared Conversations > Manage.

Proving Once Again That Apple's Approach Is Superior

Apple takes a three-tiered approach to privacy with Apple Intelligence and the all-new Siri:

  • Where possible, AI processing is done on-device
  • The first fallback is to use Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers
  • Only as a last resort is a Gemini model used, with the same PCC-level protections

The extremely sophisticated PCC architecture means neither Apple nor Google can access any data, nor is any data retained. The security architecture designed by Apple allows independent security researchers to verify this claim.
